solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Magazine missing article, one found at ground?

indicators.note: missing tells us the magazine's title is to lose a part of itself

parts.note: A long-running British weekly political magazine
the definite article is the word the

explanation.surface: A reader complains that a magazine has left out an article, perhaps one about a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The magazine's full title includes the definite article; drop it and the rest remains. A spectator watches at a sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is a person watching a match, so one is found at the sports ground.

clue.text: Sort of bush? About right

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation for right
sort here works as a verb meaning arrange, so the four letters of bush are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a plant counts as a type of bush and is told that is roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the whole clue defines and the whole clue is wordplay. 'Sort of' rearranges BUSH to SHUB, and 'About' wraps that round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A low woody plant with several stems is just what one calls a sort of bush.

clue.text: Something flowing out from eastern people probed by scholar

indicators.note: a probe goes into something, so the scholar is pushed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a nation is a people sharing a land
an MA, Master of Arts, is a holder of a degree, so a scholar

explanation.surface: A learned person investigates some people from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is a thing that issues or flows forth from a source, such as light or vapour.

clue.text: Lend out BMW wrongly in a dilapidated state

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of the preceding words are put in an incorrect order

explanation.surface: Someone lends out a BMW unwisely and gets it back battered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges the ten letters of LEND OUT BMW.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbledown describes a building falling to pieces through neglect, i.e. dilapidated.

clue.text: Bar suspended for a daredevil performance?

definitions.text: Bar suspended for a daredevil performance?

parts.words: Bar suspended for a daredevil performance?
parts.note: read literally: a horizontal bar hung from ropes high above a circus ring for acrobats to swing on

explanation.surface: A bar is closed for a while because of some reckless stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar suspended' looks like a pub shut down; it is a bar literally hanging in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: This circus apparatus is a short bar hung on ropes, used for aerial acrobatics.

clue.text: English element blocking Napoleon's way — and followers?

indicators.note: blocking means standing in the middle of the road, so these pieces sit inside the street

parts.note: Napoleon was French, and rue is French for street, a way
tin is a chemical element

explanation.surface: An English element obstructs the French emperor's route, as do his followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Napoleon's' signals a French word: rue, street.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the band of attendants who follow an important person.

clue.text: Baggage money

definitions.meaning: an old disparaging word for a brazen or impudent woman

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are slang: brass is money in northern England and also a term for a hussy, as baggage is.

clue.text: Spirited male to oppose foreign money

definitions.meaning: a dashing young man, or a male deer or rabbit
as in going against the trend

explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: a lively young man or male animal, the verb meaning resist, and American slang for a dollar.

clue.text: An amount of money granted in discussion without partner?

indicators.note: a discussion is spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a loan is a sum of money advanced to someone

explanation.surface: A grant of money is being talked over by someone who has no partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's own means having no companion or partner.

clue.text: Writer and chef on stream

parts.note: Rick Stein is a well-known British TV chef
beck is a northern English word for a stream

explanation.surface: A writer and a cook are sitting beside a brook.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the chef above the stream. John Steinbeck wrote The Grapes of Wrath.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck was an American novelist, so an example of a writer.

clue.text: Obscure almanac covers where ruler holds sway?

indicators.note: covers means the run of letters is concealed within the clue's words

explanation.surface: An obscure almanac describes the territory a monarch governs.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, the domain over which a king or queen reigns.

clue.text: Take choir after training for Jerusalem, perhaps

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so the letters of the two words are reformed

explanation.surface: A choir is taken to perform the hymn Jerusalem after rehearsals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerusalem' suggests the hymn sung by choirs; it is the Jerusalem artichoke, a root vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jerusalem artichoke is a kind of this vegetable, so 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: Vegetables including potato encapsulating starters in local lunch? Certainly

indicators.note: including means the vegetables take the rest inside them

parts.note: beans are vegetables

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing, so the potato wraps round the initials

parts.note: yam is the US name for a sweet potato

indicators.note: starters are the first courses, so the opening letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A local lunch begins with vegetables and potato; would you like some? Certainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potato' here is the sweet potato, called a yam in the US; 'starters' are not restaurant dishes but the opening letters of the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic yes, a courteous way of saying of course.

clue.text: Fit of emotion, we hear, for bird

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is to be taken by sound, not spelling

parts.note: a turn is a sudden shock or nervous attack, as in 'gave me a turn'

explanation.surface: Someone hears of a bird suffering an emotional outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: The tern is a slender seabird with forked tail, related to gulls.

clue.text: Drink is obtained beneath select feature of castle

indicators.note: in a down clue beneath puts the word is below the selection

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
to cull is to pick out, select

explanation.surface: Someone notes that drink is to be had below the chosen part of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A portcullis is the heavy grille lowered to close a castle gateway.

clue.text: Trick from rotten chap taking in retired lord

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so the chap encloses the lord

parts.note: a swine is a contemptible man

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A rogue cons a peer who has stepped down.
explanation.definitionFit: To swindle is to cheat someone, to trick them out of money.

clue.text: Distinctive ending to letter?

definitions.meaning: a name written by hand at the foot of a letter

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for something characteristic and the handwritten name that closes a letter.

clue.text: Reason to go after drug is exciting

indicators.note: to go after places the reason following the drug

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a motive is a reason for acting

explanation.surface: A reason for taking a drug is the excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotive means arousing strong feeling, so stirring or exciting.

clue.text: An Italian brought up in appeal by a lover

indicators.note: in places the turned-round piece inside the word for appeal

parts.note: it is slang for sex appeal

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means raised from bottom to top, so read upwards

parts.note: an is the article a
a Roman is an Italian, from Rome

explanation.surface: An Italian man is raised in appeal by a woman who loves him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeal' as IT is sex appeal, from the 1920s 'It girl'; 'by a' simply places the final A after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a female sweetheart, from the Italian for a woman in love.

clue.text: Group to consider reportedly part of ship

parts.note: a gang is a group of people

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard said rather than written

parts.note: to weigh is to consider carefully

explanation.surface: A team is asked to assess, as reported, some part of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangway is a passage on a ship or the movable bridge for boarding one.

clue.text: Arch yet flustered person on board?

indicators.note: flustered means agitated and confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An archly flustered sailor stands on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A yachter sails a yacht, so is a person on board a boat.

clue.text: Some tennis again a disappointment

parts.note: a set is a unit of play in tennis
back means returned, as in back again

explanation.surface: Losing part of a tennis match once more is discouraging.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a reversal of progress, which is a letdown.

clue.text: Impudent conduct upset sister in part of service?

parts.note: sauce is cheek, impudence

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the abbreviation reads upwards

explanation.surface: Cheeky behaviour upsets a nun during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like a church service; it is a tea service.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea service, a set of crockery, includes saucers as well as cups.

clue.text: A negative reaction after finding river, foreign river

indicators.note: after finding sets the reaction following the river

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
no is a negative response

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a river and says no to another one abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arno is the river flowing through Florence and Pisa in Italy.

clue.text: A set of four henchmen rose for former statesman

indicators.note: in a down clue rose means went upwards, so the run reads in reverse
a set of letters means a run taken out of the words

explanation.surface: A group of four bodyguards stood up for a past political leader.
explanation.walkthrough: fOUR HENchmen holds URHEN; 'rose' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister, a statesman of the past.

clue.text: Very ethical university soul upset after councillor is beset by drink

indicators.note: after puts the university and soul following the beset councillor
beset means surrounded, so the drink goes around the councillor

parts.note: to sup is to drink
Cllr or Cr is the abbreviation for councillor

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of soul are disordered

explanation.surface: A highly principled academic is distressed when a local councillor is surrounded by alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrupulous means having strict moral principles, extremely careful to do right.

clue.text: Number of clues forwarded for audience

indicators.note: an audience listens, so the word is taken as heard

parts.note: sent means dispatched, forwarded

explanation.surface: Puzzle clues are passed on to listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: A trail of evidence that leads a hunter or detective is a scent, hence 'number of clues'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent is a trail of traces to follow, as a detective is on the scent.

clue.text: Support rugby player

definitions.meaning: something that holds up a structure
a forward in the front row of a rugby scrum

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a structural support and a front-row forward in rugby.

clue.text: Woman guiding visitors in house?

parts.note: house here means a theatre or cinema auditorium, where a woman shows the audience to their seats

explanation.surface: A female guide shows tourists round a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' suggests a home; in theatres the auditorium is the house.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a woman employed to show people to their seats in a cinema or theatre.

clue.text: Renounce permission

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to abandon something and also authorised absence or consent.

clue.text: Sally after end of exercise gets fit

indicators.note: after places the sally following that final letter
end of picks the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a sally is a witty remark, a quip

explanation.surface: Sally finishes her workout and is in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name; it is a witticism.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit out is to equip, supplying what is needed.

clue.text: Man in second exam is not accommodating

indicators.note: in puts the man inside the second exam

parts.note: a resit is an exam taken a second time
Stan is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man retaking an exam refuses to cooperate.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistant means opposed and unyielding, the opposite of accommodating.
